description: A five-row, three-column composite figure mixing SEM and TEM micrographs of a low-density δ-ferrite steel before rolling and after rolling at four temperatures. Column 1 is SEM (scale bars 25 µm in (a), 10 µm in d/g/j/m); columns 2 and 3 are TEM with 1 µm and 500 nm scale bars respectively. (a) shows the hot-forged pre-rolling control (labelled Martensite/Austenite and δ-Ferrite) with no obvious lamellae; (b,c) confirm coarse δ-ferrite with martensite/austenite. (d-f) R650: SEM shows a banded Carbide/Ferrite lamella against δ-Ferrite (ND/RD arrows, 1 µm inset); TEM (e) shows dark spheroidal carbides inside Ferrite bounded by a red dashed line labelled Boundary; (f) carries an inset histogram titled "Carbide size: 158.3±76.9 nm". (g-i) R750: same lamellar arrangement but coarser, sparser carbides; (i) inset titled "Carbide size: 247.3±86.8 nm". (j-l) R850 and (m-o) R950: spherical carbides are absent and the lamellae are replaced by Martensite plus Ferrite in δ-Ferrite, forming honeycomb martensite lamellae with equiaxed ferrite grains that grow with temperature. The panels jointly argue that low-temperature rolling generates ultra-fine spherical carbide/ferrite composite lamellae while high-temperature rolling eliminates them.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of the steel before hot rolling, 25 µm scale bar. Coarse grains labelled 'Martensite/Austenite' in the upper region and 'δ-Ferrite' below; needle/plate-like features, no obvious lamellar banding.
TEM micrograph of the pre-rolling condition, 1 µm scale bar. Dark polygonal grains with internal dislocation lines; no lamellae or carbides visible.
TEM micrograph of the pre-rolling condition, 500 nm scale bar, labelled 'Martensite/Austenite' (upper) and 'δ-Ferrite' (lower); banded/needle contrast.
SEM of R650, 10 µm scale bar, with ND/RD orientation arrows. Labels 'Carbide/Ferrite' (banded lamella) and 'δ-Ferrite'; inset with 1 µm scale bar showing finely dispersed particles.

TEM of R650, 1 µm scale bar. Dark spherical carbides (arrow 'Carbide') dispersed in 'Ferrite'; the ferrite lamella is separated from 'δ-Ferrite' by a red dashed line labelled 'Boundary', which is nearly free of carbides.

TEM of R650, 500 nm scale bar, showing densely distributed nano-scale spherical carbides. Inset bar histogram titled 'Carbide size: 158.3±76.9 nm' with a fitted curve; histogram axis tick labels are not legible.
SEM of R750, 10 µm scale bar, labelled 'Carbide/Ferrite' and 'δ-Ferrite'; lamellar banding still present with sparse white particle contrast.
TEM of R750, 1 µm scale bar. Round carbides noticeably larger and fewer than in (f).
TEM of R750, 500 nm scale bar, with coarse carbides. Inset bar histogram titled 'Carbide size: 247.3±86.8 nm' with fitted curve; axis tick labels not legible.
SEM of R850, 10 µm scale bar. Honeycomb-like morphology labelled 'δ-Ferrite' (upper), 'Martensite' (middle) and 'Ferrite' (arrowed). No spherical carbide contrast.
TEM of R850, 1 µm scale bar, labelled 'Ferrite' (light equiaxed grains) embedded in 'Martensite'.
TEM of R850, 500 nm scale bar; equiaxed light grains (ferrite) with internal dislocation structure.
SEM of R950, 10 µm scale bar; honeycomb structure labelled 'δ-Ferrite', 'Martensite' and 'Ferrite' (arrowed), with coarser cells than (j).
TEM of R950, 1 µm scale bar, labelled 'Ferrite' (light polygon) surrounded by 'Martensite'.
TEM of R950, 500 nm scale bar; large relatively clean grains with sparse dislocations and no second-phase particles.

observations.observation: The figure is a 15-panel composite: 5 SEM micrographs (one per condition) each paired with two TEM micrographs, with SEM scale bars of 25 µm (a) or 10 µm (d,g,j,m) and TEM scale bars of 1 µm and 500 nm.
Panel (a) shows the hot-forged pre-rolling material with no obvious lamellar structure and with regions labelled 'Martensite/Austenite' and 'δ-Ferrite'.
Panel (e) shows dark spherical carbides dispersed in a 'Ferrite' lamella that is separated from 'δ-Ferrite' by a red dashed line labelled 'Boundary'.
The inset histogram in panel (f) is titled 'Carbide size: 158.3±76.9 nm' for the R650 sample.
The inset histogram in panel (i) is titled 'Carbide size: 247.3±86.8 nm' for the R750 sample.
Panels (j) and (m) show a honeycomb morphology labelled 'δ-Ferrite', 'Martensite' and 'Ferrite', with no spherical carbide contrast, whereas carbides are visible in (d)-(i).
The caption states (a-c) are SEM/TEM of the microstructure before hot rolling, (d-f) R650, (g-i) R750, (j-l) R850 and (m-o) R950.
The caption attributes to R650 spherical carbides with average diameter 158.3±76.9 nm and distribution density 1.7±0.2 µm⁻² within the lamella.
The caption attributes to R750 carbide coarsening to 247.3±86.8 nm with distribution density 0.6±0.1 µm⁻², described as coarse carbides at grain boundaries plus fine carbides inside grains.
The citing text states that before rolling the microstructure comprises coarse δ-ferrite with M/A (martensite/austenite) constituents and no obvious lamellar structure, matching panels (a-c).

The citing text states that in R650 spherical carbides show high density and ultra-fine size within the lamella while the δ-ferrite lamellae contain few carbides, consistent with the contrast in panels (d-f).

The citing text states that in the high-temperature rolling zone (R850, R950) spherical carbides disappear completely and the original lamellae are replaced by honeycomb martensite lamellae, with deformation-induced equiaxed ferrite grains growing as rolling temperature increases.
The citing text states that the R750 specimen has significantly lower carbide content and coarser particle size than R650, which is linked to a ~60% decrease in impact absorption energy.

Both inset histograms (f, i) have unreadable x- and y-axis tick labels at the supplied resolution; only their titles are legible, so the plotted distributions cannot be independently quantified from the pixels.
